ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image shows two Lewis diagrams labeled Structure A and Structure B. In Structure A, sulfur (S) is in the center with four oxygen atoms attached above, below, left, and right. Each S–O connection in Structure A is drawn as a single bond, and there are no lone-pair dots shown on the sulfur atom. The question asks specifically for the molecular geometry in Structure A. Reasoning: Around the central sulfur in Structure A, there are four bonding electron groups from the four S–O single bonds and zero lone pairs on sulfur. By VSEPR theory, a central atom with four electron groups and no lone pairs is AX4, which has tetrahedral molecular geometry.
